objects.description: Node structure for a compiled mini-regular-expression. Each node encodes an opcode in 'type' (e.g., CHAR, STAR) and either a character ('u.ch') or a pointer to a character class buffer ('u.ccl'). Used as elements of a compiled pattern array managed by the caller.
Alias type for a pointer to regex_t, representing a compiled regex node or the head of a compiled pattern. Note: this is already a pointer typedef; most APIs take re_t directly, not re_t*.

functions.name: re_matchp
functions.signature: int re_matchp(re_t pattern, const char* text, size_t text_length, size_t max_match_length, size_t* matchlength);
functions.description: Find matches of a previously compiled regular expression within the given text buffer. Intended usage: compile a pattern with re_compile into a caller-provided regex buffer, then call re_matchp to attempt a match against a non–null-terminated text buffer of length text_length. On completion, matchlength is set to the length (in bytes) of the match; the exact semantics of which match is reported and the meaning of the return value are not documented here and remain unknown from this header. Note: '.' may or may not match newlines depending on RE_DOT_MATCHES_NEWLINE (defaults to 1 in this header).
requirements: pattern must be a valid compiled regex object produced by re_compile that remains in scope for the duration of this call (inferred from API design).
text must be non-null and point to at least text_length bytes; it need not be null-terminated (explicit from parameterization by length).
matchlength must be a non-null pointer to writable memory to receive the match length (inferred from output parameter role).
max_match_length is an upper bound on the match length; precise behavior when this bound is smaller than a possible match is not documented in this header (unknown).
Behavior with respect to newline matching depends on RE_DOT_MATCHES_NEWLINE; callers should set/know this macro at compile time if they rely on a specific behavior (from header notes).
Return value semantics (success/failure codes, or position) are not documented here; callers must consult implementation or tests to interpret the int result (unknown).

functions.name: re_compile
functions.signature: int re_compile(const char* pattern, size_t pattern_length, re_t compiled_regex, unsigned char* regex_char_buffer);
functions.description: Compile a regular expression into caller-provided storage, enabling multiple patterns to be compiled without internal static buffers. Returns ERROR_SUCCESS (0) on success, else 1. Intended usage: allocate storage for an array of regex_t objects and a character-class buffer, then pass the pattern (not necessarily null-terminated) and its length to build a compiled form referenced by compiled_regex and regex_char_buffer for subsequent matching with re_matchp.
requirements: pattern must be non-null and reference at least pattern_length bytes; it does not need to be null-terminated (explicit from parameterization by length).

compiled_regex must point to writable storage sufficient to hold the compiled regex objects; capacity should allow up to MAX_REGEXP_OBJECTS regex symbols (inferred from MAX_REGEXP_OBJECTS comment and in-place compilation design).

regex_char_buffer must point to writable storage sufficient for character class data; capacity should allow up to MAX_CHAR_CLASS_LEN bytes (inferred from MAX_CHAR_CLASS_LEN comment and in-place compilation design).
The lifetime of compiled_regex and regex_char_buffer must extend through all subsequent uses (e.g., re_matchp) that rely on the compiled pattern (inferred from API design).
Return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero (1) indicates failure; specific failure reasons are not documented here (explicit for success code, unknown for error taxonomy).

data_types.description: A raw buffer of bytes of any value and length, not necessarily UTF-8 or ASCII and not null-terminated. Used when APIs take a pointer plus an explicit length and interpret the data as opaque text or binary. Suitable for regex patterns or text haystacks that may include embedded NULs.
